title: Rewrite What Matters: Adaptive Multilingual Query Rewriting for Reasoning via Agentic Reinforcement Learning

paper.title: Rewrite What Matters: Adaptive Multilingual Query Rewriting for Reasoning via Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper.abstract: Abstract In multilingual scenarios, queries with equivalent semantics but in different languages could guide the model into different reasoning trajectories, leading to performance disparities. To mitigate this gap, previous studies typically apply a one-size-fits-all query rewriting strategy, such as translation, which overlooks the fact that different scenarios require diverse types of semantic transformations. In this paper, we propose mRewriter-R1, an agentic multilingual query rewriting framework with reinforcement learning. Unlike single-turn rewriting, mRewriter-R1 formulates multilingual query rewriting as a multi-turn sequential decision-making process, where the model dynamically performs multi-aspect optimization through adaptive operator selection. Experimental results demonstrate that mRewriter-R1 outperforms all strong multilingual rewriting baselines on different large reasoning backbones. Further analyses show that the learned policy can adaptively decide on rewriting operators according to query characteristics, exhibiting strong generalization ability across diverse reasoning tasks, and plug-and-play compatibility with heterogeneous reasoning language models 1 1 1 Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/mRewriter-R1-F684 .

Affiliation: Key Laboratory of Big Data & Artificial Intelligence in Transportation(Beijing Jiaotong University), Ministry of Education Affiliation: School of Computer Science and Technology, Beijing Jiaotong University Abstract In multilingual scenarios, queries with equivalent semantics but in different languages could guide the model into different reasoning trajectories, leading to performance disparities. To mitigate this gap, previous studies typically apply a one-size-fits-all query rewriting strategy, such as translation, which overlooks the fact that different scenarios require diverse types of semantic transformations. In this paper, we propose mRewriter-R1, an agentic multilingual query rewriting framework with reinforcement learning. Unlike single-turn rewriting, mRewriter-R1 formulates multilingual query rewriting as a multi-turn sequential decision-making process, where the model dynamically performs multi-aspect optimization through adaptive operator selection. Experimental results demonstrate that mRewriter-R1 outperforms all strong multilingual rewriting baselines on different large reasoning backbones. Further analyses show that the learned policy can adaptively decide on rewriting operators according to query characteristics, exhibiting strong generalization ability across diverse reasoning tasks, and plug-and-play compatibility with heterogeneous reasoning language models 1 1 1 Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/mRewriter-R1-F684 . 1 Introduction Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities on reasoning. However, their performance has been shown to vary significantly across languages ( Huang et al., 2025 ; Shi et al., 2023 ) . This disparity is caused not only by discrepancies in various language resources but also by a high sensitivity to query understanding. In multilingual settings, queries that are semantically equivalent but differ in syntactic structure and expression across languages could guide the model into different reasoning trajectories, thereby generating inconsistent results ( Qi et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2024 ) . Therefore, adequately understanding multilingual queries via essential rewriting can align them with the correct reasoning trajectories so as to leverage the intrinsic reasoning capabilities of LLMs to improve performance for downstream tasks. Existing multilingual query rewriting (MQR) methods primarily rely on empirical manners by applying a one-size-fits-all rewriting strategy to all queries, such as full-sentence translation or word-level translation ( Kang et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2024 ; Yoo et al., 2025 ) . Such strategies cannot consistently achieve satisfactory performance for all queries in diverse scenarios and requirements. As illustrated in Figure 1 , prior methods are one-step for a single-aspect, which performs rewriting only once and fails to consider other features that may affect reasoning, such as syntactic structure ( Li et al., 2024 ) . For instance, translation helps to understand entities in some queries written in low-resource languages but hurts others that instead only require rewriting the expressions. Thus, an ideal approach is to adopt the appropriate MQR strategies at the query-level and a critical research question is whether it is possible for LLMs to dynamically learn to employ multiple MQR strategies in an adaptive way. To address this issue, the query needs to interact with LLMs continuously, leveraging the model’s reasoning process for the query at the current state to determine the most appropriate query rewriting strategy. A promising approach is to employ agentic reinforcement learning (RL) to achieve autonomous query rewriting in dynamic environments ( Jin et al., 2025 ) . However, unlike the well-defined decision of retrieval, MQR under agentic RL involves a much more open-ended action space, making stable RL substantially more challenging. It also remains unclear how to effectively integrate MQR into the agentic workflow with RL in rewriting-and-reasoning scenarios. In this paper, we propose mRewriter-R1, an agentic query rewriting framework with RL to solve multilingual reasoning tasks. Instead of relying on static and single-turn approaches, we implement a sequential decision-making paradigm where the LLM acts as both a planner and a rewriter. At each iteration, mRewriter-R1 first generates a plan based on previous turns and then performs query rewriting accordingly. Through multiple iterations, it can learn to autonomously plan the rewriting strategy and rewrite the query, improving the accuracy of the models for the multilingual reasoning. Considering the three essential aspects of a query ( i.e., how to express, how to organize, and what is truly intended ) ( Faustini et al., 2023 ) , a single-aspect rewriting strategy is insufficient to simultaneously address the corresponding challenges: eliminating expression discrepancies across languages , constructing well-structured logical forms , and understanding the underlying intent . To alleviate this, we design a multi-aspect query rewriting mechanism driven by specialized operators in a planning space. Specifically, the MQR space is categorized into three aspects: (1) Language aspect, which aims to align queries with high-resource languages via translation-based methods; (2) Structural aspect, which aims to transform complex natural language into well-structured logical expressions; and (3) Semantic aspect, which disambiguates the input and adapts it into a representation that maximizes the utilization of LLMs. Within each aspect, various multilingual rewriting strategies are encapsulated into discrete operators. This formulation constrains the inherently open-ended rewriting decision space to a finite and structured action space, thereby facilitating stable and tractable agentic RL. Subsequently, the model learns to compositionally invoke these operators, achieving combinatorial query optimization tailored to each input. Experimental results on three multilingual benchmarks demonstrate that our mRewriter-R1 framework can improve the performance of multilingual reasoning for various LLMs, consistently outperforming the static application of any single operator across all aspects. Figure 1: Illustration of the impact of query variations for multilingual reasoning. Our contributions are three-fold: (1) We propose a multi-turn Agentic RL framework that reformulates MQR into a sequential decision-making process across multiple aspects, breaking away from empirical rewriting manners. (2) The query rewriter trained by our framework mRewriter-R1 can be deployed as a plug-and-play module for the other LLMs, which is easily adapted with various backbone models and compatible with prompt-based methods such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT). (3) Experiments on different types of multilingual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that mRewriter-R1 achieves better multilingual reasoning performance compared to other baseline methods. Figure 2: The workflow of mRewriter-R1, where the policy LLM is trainable while the reference LLM is frozen. The action follows a multi-turn iteration in a sequential decision-making process with multi-aspect operator space. 2 Methods As shown in Figure 2 , we present the formal framework of mRewriter-R1, an adaptive method designed to systematically rewrite multilingual queries across language, structural, and semantic aspects. The framework follows a multi-turn decision-making manner and is optimized via outcome-based rewards to dynamically employ rewriting operators across multiple aspects. 2.1 Agentic Workflow for Multi-Turn Decision-Making We formulate MQR as a multi-turn decision-making process, where a single policy model π θ \pi_{\theta} plays two roles at each step. The model first acts as a planner to diagnose the current query and determine how it should be improved, and then acts as a rewriter to produce the updated query. Unlike conventional translation-based preprocessing, our framework allows the model to dynamically determine how the query should be rewritten through multi-aspect rollouts rather than relying on a single static transformation, optimizing multilingual queries in an adaptive and interpretable manner. Formally, this action is serialized with tags: p t = ( d t , o t ) , o t ∈ 𝒪 d t , p_{t}=(d_{t},o_{t}),\quad o_{t}\in\mathcal{O}_{d_{t}}, where o t o_{t} is the selected operator from the operator set 𝒪 d t \mathcal{O}_{d_{t}} associated with aspect d t d_{t} . Followed by the action of operator selection, the policy model performs both planning and rewriting in a unified generation process, and the transition of the query from current state to the next is defined by extracting the rewritten query from the generated action: a t ∼ π θ ( ⋅ ∣ x t , d t ) , x t + 1 = ℛ ( a t ) , a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{t},d_{t}),\quad x_{t+1}=\mathcal{R}(a_{t}), where x t x_{t} denotes the current state of queries, and ℛ \mathcal{R} denotes the rewriting operator that transforms the query into the next state. The final rewritten query x ~ \tilde{x} is generated before the downstream reasoning process starts, and is fed into a frozen downstream reasoning model after all rewriting steps are completed: y ^ = M ⁡ ( x ~ ) , x ~ = x T + 1 , \hat{y}=M(\tilde{x}),\quad\tilde{x}=x_{T+1}, where M M denotes the downstream LLMs. 2.2 Multi-Aspect Rewriting Operators As observed in the previous investigation, the failures in multilingual reasoning do not originate from a single factor. In many cases, reasoning errors are not caused by language mismatch alone, but also by implicit structural relations and ambiguous semantic expressions ( Qi et al., 2025 ) . Therefore, instead of treating rewriting as a one-step translation problem, we formulate it as a multi-aspect optimization process. However, allowing arbitrary rewriting within a single action space increases the complexity of the optimization process and makes learning more challenging.
